main_issue: Who gets to use the window corner of the shared living room (desk, laundry rack, guest seating, or Buddha altar) and whether permanent items like the desk should stay there

A-B.evidence: B: the desk is 'the main problem' and 'we all have jobs... none of us gets to claim a part of the living room' (T16, T30); A insists 'It has to be there' (T19, T26).

A-C.evidence: A and C both claim the corner for their own needs (T1, T5) but never address each other; no conflict or agreement develops afterwards.

A-D.evidence: A first said they needed the space (T1), then accepted D's wall shelf as long as it doesn't block the light; D agreed to check the position together (T9-T11): 'sounds like a plan'.

B-C.evidence: C offers to move the rack when guests come (T13); B thanks C and says 'fair enough about the laundry' (T16), though C rejected the general no-permanent-items rule (T15).

B-D.evidence: B never addresses the altar or the shelf; B's only link is the complaint that the space is still full (T12), and D does not respond to B.

C-D.evidence: D summarises C's laundry need and asks for a rearrangement that works for everyone (T6), but C never speaks to the altar or the shelf.
